request_state.literature: Literature (primary source arXiv:2412.11933, survey of solved cases): fully solved with all exponents>=3 are (3,3,n) for n<=10^9, (n,n,3) for n>=3, (n,n,n) for n>=3. Effective-finiteness only (not solved): (2p,2q,r) with p,q>=V_r [arXiv:2509.21083]. NOT solved: (4,4,5), (4,4,7), (4,6,3), any (2m,2n,r odd) with m!=n, (3,5,7), (5,5,7).
request_state.claim: COUNTERSEARCH in Z[i]: of the norm analogues of the verified Z-constraints, exactly one fails on the Helenius identity (-2+i)^3+(-2-i)^3=(1+i)^4: the lower half of no_cancellation, that the sum exceeds each summand (N(C^z)=16 < 125 = N(A^x) = N(B^y)). Every other tested analogue (upper half of no_cancellation, C-smallest exponent order, dominant dichotomy, exactly-one-even, mod-8 parity rule) HOLDS there.
